full_judgment: 7. The Judgment of the trial Court was reversed by the lower appellate Court. The lower appellate Court, we observe, while reversing the judgment of the trial Court passed its decision primarily on surmises, conjectures and assumptions without considering the material evidence on record. The trial Court found the two agreements Ext. 1 and l(a) to be genuine. The first agreement is dated 15-11-70 and no possession was delivered on that date. The second agreement is dated 31-3-73 on which date possession was delivered to the plaintiff. The lower appellate Court found that there was a material contradiction in paragraphs 4 and 5 of the plaint. But on perusal thereof we do not find any contradiction in the said two paragraphs. In paragraph 4 it is stated that defendant Nos. 1-2 returned to Bangladesh in 1972 and they accepted Taka 1500.00 from the plaintiff and in total they received 9,500.00 out of total consideration of Taka 10,000.00 keeping balance Taka 500.00 only and handed over possession to the plaintiff. This handing over of possession is relatable to the second agreement Ext. 1(a) dated 31-3-73. The recital of this agreement also speaks of handing over of possession to the plaintiff. In paragraph 5 there is a reference to the second agreement which was in confirmation of the first agreement wherein it was stipulated that the deed will be registered within six months after obtaining the necessary certificates. There is, as such, no contradiction between paragraphs 4 and 5 of the plaint. There was no assertion in the plaint that possession was delivered after the first agreement: The lower appellate Court wrongly held that, "Paragraphs 4 and 5 of the plaint contradicts about the delivery of possession and payment of consideration of Taka 1500.00" What has been stated in the plaint and adduced in evidence by the plaintiff has not at all been considered, but on pure surmises and conjectures the lower appellate Court found contradictions in paragraphs 4 and 5 of the plaint. The lower appellate Court further wrongly held that unregistered documents can be created afterwards without considering that no credible evidence was led by the defendant to show that the documents were led by a product of subsequent manipulation. The plaintiffs positive case is that these two documents Ext. 1 and 1(a) are unregistered documents and in a suit for specific performance of contract the primary question is whether the plaintiff has been able to prove the genuineness of the agreement by producing cogent reliable and independent evidence. The lower appellate Court on wrong assumptions held that tendering of money and receiving of it by defendant Nos. 1-2 as well as the second agreement are all of doubtful nature without adverting to the positive; evidence on record. The material findings of the trial Court that the agreements were genuine and consideration passed were not reversed by the lower appellate Court as a final Court of fact and hence the High Court Division rightly found that it is a proper judgment of reversal.
